source: Ported from backend/app/data/answer_key.json and backend/app/data/chart_notes.json of omer-khawar/ae-checkin-agent (Omer Khawar, MIT), 2026-10-10 (CONTRACTS.md R2.4). Everything here is SYNTHETIC: the eight notes were written for the demo in the indirect style of the Regeneron starter sheet ('pt reports 3 days of diarrhea, started loperamide'); the seventeen utterances are invented participant check-in texts. No real patient, clinician or site.
rationale: Hand-written answer key the chart-note scanner is scored against (interim_rules.chartscan.evaluate_answer_key; tests/test_chartscan.py reproduces the source repository's evaluation on the original 25 cases: AE terms precision = recall = 1.00, con-med drugs precision = recall = 1.00, every urgent/emergency case escalated, every emergency caught, zero over-escalations). Cases T18-T31 were added on 2026-10-10 after review, one per fix (each carries a review_fix note): typographic apostrophes, comma scope, review-of-systems negatives, negated or non-hospital 'admitted' / 'ED', Tmax, PRN orders, 'not started on', 'switched from X to Y'; the pass criterion stays 100% on every case. Note texts are resolved inline so the rules package is self-contained; data/synthetic/chart_notes.json carries the same eight notes for the seed and must stay identical (checked by the tests). Subject ids were remapped deterministically from the source's '101-00x' to Interim's participants 'P-00x' (last three digits -> P-<digits>), see subject_mapping. expected.escalation is the highest level the case must reach: none | human_requested | urgent | emergency (vocabulary from chartscan_red_flags.json escalation_levels); in a note every red flag counts as urgent. expected.serious is set where the text mentions a hospitalization or ER visit (possible SAE cue). The traps are deliberate: negations ('Denies fever, chills, or vomiting'), history ('Hx of migraines'), patient-education text ('educated to call for fever'), brand names ('Z-pack', 'Advil'), and the same AE appearing in two notes for one participant (N1 and N7) so cross-note de-duplication has something to link.
utterance_ref_date_note: Reference date used to turn relative onsets in utterances into dates (the source evaluator used date(2026, 10, 10)); notes use their own note_date.

cases.author: J. Rivera, NP
cases.text: Oncology follow-up. Pt reports 3 days of diarrhea, 4-5 loose stools per day, started loperamide OTC. Mild nausea persists, taking ondansetron as needed. Denies fever, chills, or vomiting. Pt educated to call for fever > 100.4 or bloody stools.

cases.review_fix: typographic apostrophe (U+2019) in an emergency red flag
cases.text: I can’t breathe and my lips are turning blue.

cases.review_fix: typographic apostrophe (U+2019) in a declined medication
cases.text: She didn’t start the prednisone they prescribed.

cases.review_fix: comma followed by a severity word ends the negation scope
cases.text: No fever, mild diarrhea for two days.

cases.review_fix: comma followed by a quantity word ends the negation scope; 'and no' continues it
cases.text: No fever and no chills, some nausea after meals.

cases.review_fix: a negated hospital word neither raises the grade nor starts the SAE clock
cases.text: Not admitted; has mild diarrhea x2 days.

cases.review_fix: review-of-systems checklist negatives ('Term: no') are post-term negations
cases.text: ROS: Nausea: no. Vomiting: no. Fever: no. Rash: yes.

cases.review_fix: 'admitted to having' is not a hospital admission
cases.text: Pt admitted to having mild nausea most mornings.
Tmax 101.3 overnight, took Tylenol.

cases.review_fix: 'PRN for <symptom>' is a standing order, not a symptom report
cases.text: Has Tylenol PRN for fever.

cases.review_fix: 'was not started on' excludes the drug
cases.text: Patient was not started on prednisone.

cases.review_fix: 'switched from X to Y' is X stopped and Y started
cases.text: Switched from Zofran to Compazine yesterday.

cases.review_fix: 'in the ED' is a hospital cue; bare 'ED' is not
cases.text: Seen in the ED yesterday for vomiting, sent home.

cases.review_fix: 'go to the ER if' is an instruction: no hospital cue, no dehydration flag (U+2019 apostrophe)
cases.text: Go to the ER if you can’t keep fluids down.
